subject: architecture
statement: Each SpacetimeDB database is a single-threaded actor: reducers execute serially in-memory against tables, with durability via a commit log + snapshots. Throughput comes from no network hop between logic and data, not from parallelism.

subject: architecture
statement: Reducers are transactional: any panic/Err rolls back every write in that call. Duplication bugs from half-applied trades are structurally prevented when the whole operation is one reducer.

subject: architecture
statement: Clients receive state through SQL subscriptions; the server pushes row inserts/deletes (updates = delete+insert by primary key) as each transaction commits, and the SDK maintains a client-side cache.

subject: architecture
statement: Modules can be written in Rust, C#, TypeScript (V8) or C++; clients exist for Rust, C#/Unity, TypeScript/React, Unreal (C++/Blueprint) plus community GDScript (Godot), Elixir and others.

subject: architecture
statement: Procedures (beta) are the only module functions allowed to do outbound HTTP; they are not transactional by default and must open explicit transactions to write tables.

subject: architecture
statement: Views are read-only module functions clients can subscribe to, useful for per-player projections and hiding information.

subject: architecture
statement: Row-level security / client-visibility filters let a module restrict which rows a given identity can see in subscriptions; combine with private tables for hidden information.

subject: architecture
statement: ctx.sender() (Identity) is the only trustworthy caller identity in a reducer; clients never pass their own player id as an argument.

subject: architecture
statement: Scheduled tables (a table with scheduled(reducer) + ScheduleAt column) are the only timer mechanism: insert a row to schedule, the reducer fires with that row; repeat by Interval or re-insert.

subject: architecture
statement: Publishing a new module version is hot-swap: clients stay connected; additive schema changes migrate automatically, destructive ones need --delete-data (wipe) or a manual migration plan.

subject: license
statement: SpacetimeDB server is BSL 1.1 (Licensed Work = 2.14.0). Additional Use Grant: production use allowed for an application using no more than ONE SpacetimeDB instance in production, and not as a Database Service. Change Date 2031-10-25 -> AGPLv3 with linking exception.

subject: license
statement: Self-hosting a sharded MMO (root + N region databases on a multi-node deployment) likely exceeds 'one SpacetimeDB instance in production' and needs a commercial license or Maincloud; multiple databases inside one standalone instance are a different question - ask Clockwork Labs before launch.
evidence: BSL Additional Use Grant wording; whether 'instance' = process or database is not defined in the grant

subject: license
statement: Subdirectories with their own LICENSE are Apache-2.0: docs/, crates/bindings*, sdks/*, templates/*, demo/Blackholio, modules/*, codex-plugin/. The repo-root skills/ folder has no own LICENSE, so it falls under BSL; the identical skills under codex-plugin/ are Apache-2.0.
evidence: LICENSE.txt section 2 + per-directory LICENSE files in the master tree

subject: license
statement: BitCraftPublic (server source of BitCraft Online) is Apache-2.0: patterns and code may be reused with attribution and NOTICE.

subject: license
statement: The flametime Godot GDScript SDK and its plaught-armor hard fork are MIT; vendoring or patching them is allowed with the copyright notice retained.

subject: license
statement: TES3MP is GPLv3: never copy its code into an Apache/MIT kit; only ideas (state authority split, packet categories) may inform designs.

subject: license
statement: Vendor blog posts, essays and release notes carry no open license: the kit should link to them and paraphrase, not copy.

subject: scale
statement: Clockwork Labs' benchmark (account-transfer transactions end-to-end) reports ~300k TPS (303,920 TPS in the 2026-05-14 run); replicated databases reach the same throughput given enough bandwidth.

subject: scale
statement: Benchmark TPS (tiny transfer reducers) does not translate to MMO capacity; game cost is dominated by subscription fan-out (rows x subscribers x update rate) and per-tick reducer work. Measure your own workload.

subject: scale
statement: BitCraft runs a root/global database plus spatial region databases; regions execute in parallel and players move between region databases. This is the vendor-blessed MMO scale-out pattern.

subject: scale
statement: BitCraft reported lag at roughly 500-700 players in one region at launch; plan a working ceiling of ~500 concurrent active players per region database until your own load test says otherwise.
evidence: research spike 2026-10-30 (BitCraft launch reports + vendor statements); see scale facts

subject: scale
statement: BitCraft's Steam concurrent peak was ~4.4k players spread over ~9 region databases plus a global database - evidence that region sharding, not one big database, is how a live STDB MMO reaches thousands.
evidence: SteamDB peak + BitCraft region count (research spike 2026-10-30)

subject: scale
statement: Vendor scale roadmap: (1) replicated databases - shipped; (2) async inter-database communication - Oct 31 2026; (3) tiered storage - Oct 31 2026; (4) read replicas - planned; (5) sync IDC / cross-db transactions - planned; (6) intra-database partitioning - planned.

subject: scale
statement: v2.14.0 (2026-10-30) ships async inter-database calls for Rust and TypeScript modules: dependencies declared in spacetime.json, insert-only outbox tables, an HTTP/2 delivery actor and on_result callbacks. Delivery is currently same-host/localhost only.

subject: scale
statement: Tiered storage was announced for the Oct 31 2026 launch but is not in the 2.14.0 release notes; treat it as not shipped until a release lists it.
evidence: v2.14.0 notes vs blog roadmap; PRs #6304 'Tiered storage base' and #6305 'Integrate tiered storage' still open as of 2026-10-30

subject: scale
statement: Without sync IDC there are no cross-database transactions: a player handoff between region databases must be an idempotent multi-step protocol (lock -> offer -> accept -> delete source -> activate) that tolerates retries and partial failure.
evidence: IDC design (async, at-least-once outbox) + BitCraft handoff code

subject: scale
statement: All in-memory: table data must fit in RAM of the host; size large static world data (terrain, item defs) deliberately and keep cold history out of hot tables until tiered storage ships.

subject: scale
statement: Since 2.13, HTTP reducer calls wait for durability; a 504 means the outcome is unknown, so any externally-triggered reducer must be idempotent (request ids / dedup table).

subject: scale
statement: Small-scale reference point: Classic open-source multiplayer mods typically see tens of concurrent real players; a Godot+STDB hobby MMO should first prove 50-100 bots before chasing 1,000+.
evidence: TES3MP community numbers; local staged scale plan

subject: scale
statement: A staged load plan that worked locally: Stage 1 = 10 humans/bots functional; Stage 2 = 100 bots with budgets; Stage 3 = 1,000 bots on one region; Stage 4 = 5,000 bots across regions with handoff.

subject: versions
statement: Pin exact SpacetimeDB versions (CLI, server, module crate, client SDK) per project; never float 'latest'. Upgrade server before modules for 2.14 (is_internal semantics changed).

subject: versions
statement: Never open the only copy of a database's data directory with a newer server binary; upgrades are one-way. Copy the data dir, run the new binary side-by-side on a different port, verify, then cut over.

subject: versions
statement: Rust modules on 2.13+ need a recent toolchain (MSRV 1.97, pin an exact toolchain such as 1.97.1); pin with rust-toolchain.toml in the module folder.

subject: versions
statement: 2.12 rejects HS256-signed JWTs (use RS256/ES256 OIDC issuers), deduplicates scheduler entries, adds Rust module test utilities and C#/TS client auto-reconnect.

subject: versions
statement: 2.10.2 canonicalized database namespaces; 2.11 improved publish/update diagnostics (schema-change explanations).

subject: versions
statement: Official agent support: spacetimedb.com/agent-setup.md, /llms.txt, /.well-known/agent-skills/index.json, an MCP server and per-language SKILL.md files (cli, concepts, rust-server, typescript-server, csharp-server, cpp-server, typescript-client, csharp-client, unity, unreal, mcp).

subject: client
statement: The Godot GDScript SDK (flametime 0.2.x, 2.3.0+) requires a primary key on every table for the client cache; tables without one only fire insert/delete callbacks and are not stored.

subject: client
statement: The GDScript SDK does not ref-count overlapping subscriptions; AOI code should subscribe/unsubscribe per cell (one query set per chunk) rather than re-issuing a big overlapping query.

subject: client
statement: Brotli compression is not supported by the Godot SDK; use NONE or GZIP.

subject: client
statement: Isolate the SDK behind one seam (e.g. Net.gd / net.ts) that owns connect, subscribe, reducer calls and reconnect; gameplay code reads the local cache only. This made SDK forks/upgrades and bot clients cheap.

subject: client
statement: Rust/C# SDK clients must pump messages (frame_tick / run_threaded / FrameTick in Unity Update); forgetting it looks like 'connected but no data'.

subject: process
statement: Agents writing STDB Rust modules hallucinate APIs from pre-1.0 and other crates at a high rate; a checked-in rules file with a 'wrong vs right' catalog plus a compile gate is the most effective mitigation.
evidence: template server/CLAUDE.md catalog; repeated local fixes

subject: process
statement: Two-identity tests (two separate client identities) catch most authority bugs: unauthorized joins, cross-player writes and idempotent grants.

subject: process
statement: Revoking a player's access in tables does not close an existing websocket; enforce admission in every reducer (and on connect) or restart/kick, otherwise a revoked client keeps its live subscription.

subject: process
statement: init only runs on first publish; additive publishes do not re-run it. Seed/backfill new tables with idempotent ensure_* reducers or a migration-version table.

subject: process
statement: A load-test gate with budgets.json (p95 tick ms, reducer ms, subscription bytes/s, must_plateau memory) and a PASS/CONCERNS/FAIL verdict stopped regressions reaching playtests.

subject: process
statement: Off-tick heavy compute (pathfinding, mob AI, mapgen) worked best in a native sidecar process connected as a privileged SDK client that commits results through service-gated reducers.
